policy.note: Curated shelf for an AI-era entrepreneur. Not a bookstore. Phase 2 UI will read this file; MVP does not show Library yet.

books.title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
books.author: Ben Horowitz
books.why: Company-building when things break — closer to real founder life than inspirational startup Twitter.
books.when: After you have (or are about to have) something real to operate.
books.action: Write down your top 3 'hard things' if this business got real in 90 days.

books.title: High Output Management
books.author: Andrew S. Grove
books.why: Leverage, indicators, and meetings that don't waste life — works for solo ops and small teams.
books.when: When your time is the bottleneck (already true on the road).
books.action: Pick one weekly metric that would prove your AI idea is working.

books.title: Inspired
books.author: Marty Cagan
books.why: How strong product orgs decide what to build — antidote to feature theater.
books.when: Before you pour months into an AI feature nobody asked for.
books.action: Interview 3 people with the pain you think AI solves; write what they actually do today.

books.title: Traction
books.author: Gabriel Weinberg & Justin Mares
books.why: Distribution channels checklist — AI products still die from no customers, not no model.
books.when: When you have a wedge and need first users/revenue.
books.action: Score 3 traction channels you can run from a phone between loads.

books.title: Obviously Awesome
books.author: April Dunford
books.why: Positioning so buyers get it in one sentence — critical in a noisy AI market.
books.when: When you can demo something but can't explain why you vs ChatGPT-generic.
books.action: Draft one positioning line: for [who] who [pain], we [difference].

books.title: Power and Prediction
books.author: Ajay Agrawal, Joshua Gans, Avi Goldfarb
books.why: Economics of prediction/AI — where value and power actually move.
books.when: Early — shapes which problems are businesses vs demos.
books.action: Name one decision in freight/logistics where better prediction is worth real money.

books.title: Designing Machine Learning Systems
books.author: Chip Huyen
books.why: How ML products work in production — enough literacy to not get snowed by vendors.
books.when: When you start buying/building anything beyond a thin API wrapper.
books.action: List data you already touch (loads, rates, customers) that could feed a system.

books.title: The Lean Startup
books.author: Eric Ries
books.why: Build–measure–learn without burning a year. Classic for a reason; skim if you already live it.
books.when: If you tend to overbuild before talking to users.
books.action: Define a 2-week MVP you could validate without quitting trucking.

books.title: Crossing the Chasm
books.author: Geoffrey A. Moore
books.why: B2B adoption reality — early fans ≠ mainstream buyers. Matters for enterprise AI.
books.when: If you sell to businesses (brokers, fleets, shippers), not consumers.
books.action: Identify your beachhead customer in one niche, not 'everyone in logistics.'

books.title: Hooked
books.author: Nir Eyal
books.why: Habit loops for products — use ethically; useful if you build tools people open daily.
books.when: When designing something you want users to return to (like this Pulse).
books.action: Map trigger → action → reward for one product idea.
